dedupe_keys.name: igs ionosphere vertical total electron content vtec maps final product from nasa cddis

description: This NASA Earthdata catalog entry describes the IGS final global ionosphere maps of vertical total electron content (VTEC), derived daily from a global network of GNSS ground receivers. The IGS Ionosphere Analysis Center Coordinator combines solutions from several analysis centres into the official maps, which have a resolution of 2 hours in universal time, 5 degrees in longitude and 2.5 degrees in latitude, and are available with a latency of 11 days. The files, in IONEX format, also carry delay code bias values for GNSS satellites and ground receivers. The record shows global coverage from 1 January 1998 to the present, 3,270 granules, and a file naming convention by year and day. Rapid and predicted product versions have their own catalog entries. Producer: IGS through NASA CDDIS; catalog page read on 29 September 2026. Coverage: global. Access: catalog page free to browse; the data are openly shared without restriction and the download itself goes through CDDIS, which was not opened. Licence and cost: free. Caveats: coarse resolution and latency make it a post-processing product, and CDDIS pages can require an Earthdata login for some downloads. Simulation uses: the maps give ionospheric delay inputs for exposure and accuracy analysis of positioning services. Related records: IGS GNSS products (data-igs-gnss-products), which covers the wider IGS product set, ESA Navigation Support Office GNSS products (data-esa-navigation-support-office-gnss-products) and the CAS TECRecon global ionospheric maps (data-cas-tecrecon30-global-ionospheric-maps).
